tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description explicitly instructs when to use the skill ('Use when a user asks to audit or review CloudTrail coverage...'), lists many explicit trigger contexts phrased around user intent (asking about audit, logging, record of actions, trail/region coverage, org trail, Event history sufficiency), and also explicitly carves out what it is NOT for. It is dense but still a single well-structured paragraph, appropriate given the need to disambiguate from a similarly named cost-optimization skill.
tests.evidence: "Use when a user asks to audit or review CloudTrail coverage, says auditors need to know what is logged, asks if CloudTrail would record an action like an object delete, which resources lack data events... Not for CloudTrail cost or charges, who did what or event searches, CIS or Security Hub scoring, or changing a trail or selector."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific, non-obvious facts (coverage state definitions, organization trail ARN quirks, rating roll-up rules) and does not waste space explaining general concepts like what CloudTrail or S3 are. It assumes the agent already knows AWS basics and jumps straight into project-specific procedures and edge cases.
tests.evidence: 'Organization trails by full ARN, always. A failed name call is a mistake to retry, never a permission boundary.'

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (API call shapes, full check matrix descriptions, report template, permissions table) is consistently delegated to references/ files and only summarized briefly in the body, including inside conditional branches like organization trail handling.
tests.evidence: 'Full definitions, narrowing labels and which check (D4 or M3) carries each, selector semantics, Region scope, Lake stores and worked examples: [coverage-model.md](references/coverage-model.md), read with read_skill_resource before Step 6.'

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ are linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a clear trigger condition for when to load it (specific step number or specific error condition).
tests.evidence: '[permissions.md](references/permissions.md), read with read_skill_resource on the first AccessDenied.'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (ARN calls, selector classification, rating roll-up) are given exact prescriptive steps, while sections like Known Quirks and rationale for the Relay Rule explain purpose, calibrating specificity to fragility appropriately.
tests.evidence: 'Call GetTrailStatus and GetEventSelectors once each with the full TrailARN, never the name (a name call returns TrailNotFoundException and proves nothing).'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: No competing tool options are presented without a clear default; the skill specifies exact single API calls and sequences rather than offering alternative tools.
tests.evidence: Skill does not present multiple approaches/tools as equal choices anywhere in the body.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (account scope resolution, coverage model mapping, fixed 20-check matrix) that applies to any CloudTrail audit request, not a one-off declarative task.
tests.evidence: 'Every in scope resource gets exactly one state, first match wins: 1. NotApplicable... 2. Unknown... 3. Covered...'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The Known Quirks section documents concrete, non-obvious environment facts (Event history limitations, service-linked role session attribution) that the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: 'Event history is 90 days, management events only, one Region per search, and independent of trails; it never answers a data event or retention question.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides an output template reference and defines report structure, satisfying the need for structured output in an audit report.
tests.evidence: 'The final message to the user is the full report defined in [report-template.md](references/report-template.md), sections in order: Scope, Coverage Rating...'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body does not inline a large template; instead it summarizes the required sections briefly and delegates the full template to report-template.md in references/.
tests.evidence: 'The final message to the user is the full report defined in [report-template.md](references/report-template.md), sections in order: Scope, Coverage Rating (with Bottom line), Resource Coverage, Next Steps, Trail Inventory, Findings, Check Matrix, What Auditors Should Know, Not Assessed.'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-check section instructing the agent to validate its own output (counts, row counts, denied calls) before sending the final report.
tests.evidence: 'Self check before sending (full list: report-template.md). Counts match across Coverage Rating, Bottom line and Resource Coverage; the Check Matrix has exactly 20 rows; every Uncovered row was reached only after every readable source was evaluated...'
